section: Decoding the interfacial structure and functionality of an organic additive for superconformal cobalt electrodeposition
text: Zijie Mao 1, Xianglong Du 2, Xindi Xu 1, Yicai Wu 1, Xiaohui Yang 2* Kun Jiang 1, Jun Cheng 2, Zhi-You Zhou 2, Shi-Gang Sun 2 & Wen-Bin Cai.1* Received January 7, 2025; accepted March 9, 2025; published online May 6, 2025 Cobalt (Co) metallization presents a promising alternative strategy for the bottom interconnect in advanced chip manufacture, yet the interfacial structure and functionality ofan organic additive essential for superconformal Co deposition is far from clear given the concurring hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Herein, interfacial electrochemistry for a model additive molecule MBIS (sodium 2-mercapto-5-benzimidazolesulfonate) at a Co electrode is investigated by applying in situ surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy and electrochemical quartz crystal microbalance combined with density functional theory calculations The vertical plane adsorption of MBIS on the Co surface via thiolate reduces the overall reduction current with a higher/lower Faradaic efficiency (FE) towards HER/Co deposition due to the significant blockage of surface Co sites as well as the formation of Co(II) complex with MBIS.

unit_id: 解码添加剂界面结构性能#0006
section: Decoding the interfacial structure and functionality of an organic additive for superconformal cobalt electrodeposition > 1 Introduction
text: Cu is the most commonly used interconnect metal by means of Damascene Cu plating, however, when a 14-nm (or below) process is adopted, electron scattering at external surfaces and grain boundaries leads to a sharp rise in the resistance of narrow Cu lines in the bottom layers [6]. At the nanoscale, the resistivity of a metal is directly related to ρ _b × λ, where ρ _b represents the bulk resistivity of the metal and λ represents the electron mean free path [7,8]. Co, Ru, Rh, and Mo have lower ρ _b × λ values and thus are expected to exhibit lower resistances in narrow lines.

In particular, Co interconnect by electrodeposition is highly promising for commercial applications because of its low cost and relative ease for plating among the four alternative metals [10,11].

text: Unlike acidic Cu electroplating in which hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) is negligible, Co electroplating is accompanied by HER given that φ _Co ^2 + / Co = - 0.2 8 : V vs. SHE and φ_H^+/H_2=0 : V vs. SHE [12,13]. In order to achieve bottom-up filling and avoid voids in the vias, a suitable inhibiting additive, such as sodium 2-mercapto-5-benzimidazolesulfonate (MBIS) [14], or dimethylglyoxime among others [15–25], is needed to regulate the kinetics of Co deposition.

Several superfilling (superconformal deposition) models have been proposed to account for the additive-assisted filling process, including the S-shaped negative differential resistance (S-NDR) [15,26,27], the differential current efficiency fill (DCEF) model [28,29], and the hydrogen reduction-induced deactivation (HID) model [30,31].

text: Several superfilling (superconformal deposition) models have been proposed to account for the additive-assisted filling process, including the S-shaped negative differential resistance (S-NDR) [15,26,27], the differential current efficiency fill (DCEF) model [28,29], and the hydrogen reduction-induced deactivation (HID) model [30,31]. Notably, despite their significant achievement from a simulation perspective, these models lack a molecular-level insight into the interaction of a specific organic additive with a Co electrode as well as its impact on the Co electrodeposition, which is otherwise highly demanded for the mechanistic understanding and design ofadvanced additives.

section: Decoding the interfacial structure and functionality of an organic additive for superconformal cobalt electrodeposition > 1 Introduction
text: In this work, MBIS, an organic additive already validated for nano-vias Co superfilling [14], is selected as the target model molecule. The interfacial structure and mechanistic aspect of adsorbed MBIS at the Co electrode are probed initially by high sensitivity in situ ATR-SEIRAS and DFT calculations. Electrochemical quartz crystal microbalance (EQCM) is applied to quantify the relative contributions of Co deposition and HER in the Co-plating solutions with and without the additive.

text: In this study, we have delved into the inhibition mechanism of the additive MBIS in acidic Co electroplating using a synergistic approach inclusive of electrochemical and ATR-SEIRAS measurement as well as computational simulations. The MBIS molecule adapts a nearly vertical adsorption configuration on the Co electrode via the formation of thiolate, reducing both partial currents for Co deposition and H _ 2 evolution with a higher FE _ Co and a lower FE _ H _ 2,, as compared to the MBIS-free case.
